summary.headline: Olectra Q2 FY27 revenue rose only 4.6% to ₹687 crore, though H1 revenue grew 25.8% to ₹1,262.5 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 16%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was ₹687 crore, up 4.6% YoY, while Q2 EBITDA rose 18.2% to ₹109.9 crore with margin up to 16% from 14.2%. H1 revenue grew 25.8% to ₹1,262.5 crore and H1 EBITDA rose 22.7% to ₹182.8 crore, but margin eased to 14.5% from 14.8%. Mobility drove results: Q2 mobility segment profit rose 18.1%, and the company delivered a record 401 vehicles in the quarter, though mix shifted toward lower-priced 9-metre buses. Energy segment profit fell in Q2 and H1 despite strong revenue growth, as export mix and margins normalised.

vs cash outflow in prior year

segments.name: Mobility (electric buses)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue broadly flat YoY while H1 revenue rose about 24.7%; record 401 deliveries in Q2 and 749 in H1 vs 536 a year ago. Q2 revenue was held back by mix, with most deliveries 9-metre buses (~₹1.1 crore each vs ~₹1.45 crore for 12-metre). Management says mobility margins are back at about 14%.

segments.name: Energy (polymer/composite insulators)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% in Q2 and 37.2% in H1, but segment profit fell 6.5% in Q2 and 4.5% in H1 on lower exports and higher raw material and environmental costs. Export share was about 13% in H1 vs about 40% a year earlier; management guides to a 25-30% margin range, down from about 35% last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to keep growing at 20-25%, in line with the first half.
Management is cautiously optimistic on FY27 growth and aims for sustainable, profitable growth while managing working capital and finance costs.
Energy segment margin target of 25-30%, with export mix expected to recover by one to two points.
Tamil Nadu e-bus tender (participated via an operating partner) outcome expected this month; currently under technical evaluation.
First electric truck prototype under build; launch targeted for end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28 after extensive testing.
A 13.5-metre private-segment bus is in development and will be part of upcoming launches.
capex_capacity: Record 401 vehicle deliveries in Q2 and 749 in H1 FY27, which management said is among the highest in the company's history.
Order book about 1,500 units of 9-metre and over 3,000 units of 12-metre buses; 12-metre expected to form a larger share of future volume.
Electric truck prototype under testing, with launch planned for end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28.
Management said capacity investments support growth; no specific new facility commissioning timeline was given in the call.
Mentions of rising depreciation from capacity expansion and higher term-debt interest; debt repayments continued alongside capex.
demand_pricing: Mobility: 9-metre buses ~₹1.1 crore and 12-metre ~₹1.45 crore; Q2 mix skewed to lower-priced 9-metre units.
Olectra claims ~22%+ market share in e-buses, in the top two among about 14 players; about 13 players in e-trucks.
Energy: claims over 30% share of the polymer insulator market, with the largest revenue of ₹98 crore vs ~₹60 crore for the next player.
Market context: STU procurement ~5,100 vehicles in H1 FY27, of which ~3,700 (~70%) electric; e-bus penetration ~9% of bus registrations in H1.
Private bus demand: Fresh Bus has run five to six lakh km on the company's initial batch of buses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did energy segment margin fall from about 35% to about 25%, and how does it compare with a peer reporting around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not verify peer data and industry margins are about 25-30%. It said 35% was a peak year helped by strong export demand. It now targets a stable 25-30% range, with H1 export share at about 13% vs about 40% last year due to US trade-duty changes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue barely rise in mobility despite volumes up about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix: most Q2 deliveries were 9-metre buses at a lower price point. Mix will vary with contract timing. Order book is mixed, with 9-metre below 50%, and 12-metre volume share is expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is Olectra losing ground in e-trucks to new entrants, and what about the expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Olectra is in the top two in e-buses with ~22% share and plans to lead in trucks. It is building a prototype, with launch at end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28, and is relying on its ~750 million km of bus operating experience and 117 trucks in the market. No specific expansion details were given.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Tamil Nadu 12-metre AC e-bus tender and private bus opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: The tender is under technical evaluation, bid through an operating partner, with outcome expected this month. Engagement with Fresh Bus and other private operators continues, and a 13.5-metre bus is in development.

qa_highlights.question: Will the composite insulator business be demerged, and what is the status of GFRP rebar and related litigation?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger proposal exists yet; the board will consider it and disclose after approval. The GFRP rebar business was prototyped but dropped on margin concerns. Management said there is no litigation on the matter raised by the questioner.

risks_watch: Energy margin normalisation to 25-30% and export recovery depend on US trade duties and raw material costs.
Working capital pressure: receivables and inventory absorbed significant operating cash in H1; collections need to accelerate.
Mobility mix toward 9-metre buses may keep revenue growth lagging volume growth in the near term.
Rising depreciation and finance costs are holding PBT and PAT growth (5.1% and 4.4%) well below EBITDA growth.
Tamil Nadu tender outcome due this month; e-truck launch timing and competition from new entrants.
summary.management_tone: Confident on mobility volumes, record deliveries and the 20-25% growth target, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the energy segment's margin decline and the Q2 revenue slowdown, which management framed as mix-driven. Answers on demerger and the tender were brief and non-committal.
